paragraphs.title: Jacob Meets the Camp of God

easy.question: What did Laban do in the morning?
answers: He kissed and blessed his family
He met the angels of God
He built a new camp
easy.explanation: The verse says that Laban rose in the morning, kissed his sons and daughters, and blessed them.

easy.question: Where did Laban return?
answers: To Jacob’s camp
To his own place
To the land of Egypt
easy.explanation: At the end of the verse, it says, “And Laban returned unto his place.”

easy.question: Whom did Jacob meet on his way?
answers: Laban’s sons
The people of the city
The angels of God
easy.explanation: The verse says, “And the angels of God met him.”

medium.question: What was the correct order of events?
answers: Jacob met angels, and then Laban returned to his place
Laban parted from his family, and then Jacob met angels
Jacob named the place Mahanaim, and then met angels
medium.explanation: First Laban parted from his family and returned home. Then Jacob continued on his way and met the angels of God.

medium.question: Why did Jacob call the place “Mahanaim”?
answers: Because he saw two houses there
Because he saw God’s host there
Because Laban established two camps there
medium.explanation: Jacob saw the angels of God and said, “This is God’s host,” so he named the place Mahanaim.

medium.question: In the phrase “the angels of God met him,” what does “met” mean?
answers: They encountered him
They attacked him
They blessed him
medium.explanation: In this context, the angels appeared in Jacob’s path and encountered him; the verse does not describe an attack.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “When Jacob saw them”?
answers: Jacob saw the angels before naming the place
Laban saw the angels before leaving
The angels saw Jacob only after returning home
challenge.explanation: The verse says that Jacob named the place Mahanaim after seeing the angels of God.

challenge.question: What does the plural word “angels” indicate?
answers: Jacob met one angel
Jacob saw a group of angels
Jacob met many human beings
challenge.explanation: The plural form indicates that Jacob encountered more than one angel.

challenge.question: What does the name “Mahanaim” mean linguistically?
answers: Two camps
Two wells
Two mountains
challenge.explanation: The name Mahanaim is related to the word “camp” and suggests two camps, Jacob’s camp and God’s camp.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “When Jacob saw them”?
answers: Jacob saw the angels before naming the place
Laban saw the angels before leaving
The angels saw Jacob only after returning home
questions.explanation: The verse says that Jacob named the place Mahanaim after seeing the angels of God.

questions.question: What does the plural word “angels” indicate?
answers: Jacob met one angel
Jacob saw a group of angels
Jacob met many human beings
questions.explanation: The plural form indicates that Jacob encountered more than one angel.

questions.question: What does the name “Mahanaim” mean linguistically?
answers: Two camps
Two wells
Two mountains
questions.explanation: The name Mahanaim is related to the word “camp” and suggests two camps, Jacob’s camp and God’s camp.

easy.question: Who sent messengers to Esau?
answers: Jacob
Laban
Isaac
easy.explanation: The verse says, “And Jacob sent messengers.”

easy.question: To whom were the messengers sent?
answers: To Laban
To Esau
To Isaac
easy.explanation: The messengers were sent to Esau, Jacob’s brother.

easy.question: What did Jacob ask the messengers to do?
answers: Build a house
Buy land
Tell Esau about his situation
easy.explanation: Jacob said, “I have sent to tell my lord.”

medium.question: Why did Jacob tell Esau that he had possessions and servants?
answers: To show that he was prosperous and seek Esau’s favor
To ask Esau to give him possessions
To announce that he was returning to Egypt
medium.explanation: Jacob wanted to find favor in Esau’s sight, so he told him about his situation and possessions.

medium.question: What does “I have sojourned with Laban, and stayed there until now” mean?
answers: I fought
I lived or stayed there
I fled
medium.explanation: The phrase means that Jacob had lived with Laban and remained there until that time.

medium.question: What sequence of events is described in the verses?
answers: Esau sent messengers, and then Jacob went to Laban
Jacob gained possessions, and then messengers were sent to him
Jacob stayed with Laban, gained possessions, and sent messengers to Esau
medium.explanation: Jacob says that he lived with Laban, acquired possessions there, and then sent messengers to inform Esau.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from Jacob calling Esau “my lord” and himself “your servant”?
answers: Jacob was speaking respectfully and cautiously
Jacob had become Esau’s servant
Esau was Jacob’s father
challenge.explanation: These are expressions of respect and humility, intended to calm Esau and avoid conflict.

challenge.question: What is the meaning of “stayed there until now”?
answers: Jacob was only one day late
Jacob remained with Laban until the present time
Jacob waited for Esau to come to him
challenge.explanation: The phrase means that Jacob had stayed with Laban until then and had not returned earlier.

challenge.question: To what region were the messengers sent?
answers: Haran, the land of Laban
Egypt, the land of Pharaoh
The land of Seir, the country of Edom
challenge.explanation: The verse explicitly says that the messengers were sent to Esau in the land of Seir, the country of Edom.

questions.question: What can be inferred from Jacob calling Esau “my lord” and himself “your servant”?
answers: Jacob was speaking respectfully and cautiously
Jacob had become Esau’s servant
Esau was Jacob’s father
questions.explanation: These are expressions of respect and humility, intended to calm Esau and avoid conflict.

questions.question: What is the meaning of “stayed there until now”?
answers: Jacob was only one day late
Jacob remained with Laban until the present time
Jacob waited for Esau to come to him
questions.explanation: The phrase means that Jacob had stayed with Laban until then and had not returned earlier.

questions.question: To what region were the messengers sent?
answers: Haran, the land of Laban
Egypt, the land of Pharaoh
The land of Seir, the country of Edom
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly says that the messengers were sent to Esau in the land of Seir, the country of Edom.

paragraphs.title: Jacob Prepares for Danger and Prays

easy.question: Who returned to Jacob and told him that Esau was coming to meet him?
answers: The messengers
The shepherds
His sons
easy.explanation: The messengers returned and told Jacob that Esau was coming with four hundred men.

easy.question: Into how many camps did Jacob divide the people and possessions?
answers: Three camps
Two camps
One camp
easy.explanation: Jacob divided the people, flocks, herds, and camels into two companies.

easy.question: How many men were with Esau?
answers: Two hundred men
One hundred men
Four hundred men
easy.explanation: The messengers told Jacob that Esau was coming with four hundred men.

medium.question: Why did Jacob divide his camp into two companies?
answers: So that if one company was attacked, the other might escape
So that he could return to Haran
So that he could send one company to Esau
medium.explanation: Jacob feared that Esau would attack one company and hoped that the other would escape.

medium.question: What does “I am not worthy of the least of all the mercies” mean?
answers: I became physically small
I am not worthy of all these blessings
I lost all my possessions
medium.explanation: Jacob feels unworthy of all the goodness and faithfulness God has shown him.

medium.question: What is the correct sequence of events?
answers: Jacob prayed, the messengers returned, and then he divided the camp
Jacob divided the camp, Esau arrived, and then the messengers returned
The messengers returned, Jacob became afraid and divided the camp, and then he prayed
medium.explanation: First the messengers reported Esau’s approach. Jacob then became afraid and divided the camp, and finally prayed to God.

challenge.question: What can we learn from Jacob mentioning both God’s promise and his fear of Esau?
answers: He trusted God’s promise while also asking for help in danger
He did not believe God’s promise at all
He planned to fight Esau alone
challenge.explanation: Jacob recalled God’s promise to multiply his descendants while asking for deliverance from Esau.

challenge.question: What does Jacob emphasize by saying, “With my staff I passed over this Jordan; and now I am become two bands”?
answers: That he had never been alone
The change from poverty and simplicity to abundant possessions and family
That he wanted to divide his family permanently
challenge.explanation: Jacob recalls crossing the Jordan with only a staff, while now he has many people and possessions divided into two camps.

challenge.question: What does “lest he will come and smite me, and the mother with the children” reveal about Jacob’s fear?
answers: He feared that Esau would take only his possessions
He feared that Esau would ask him to return to Haran
He feared the complete destruction of his family, including mothers and children
challenge.explanation: Jacob feared that Esau would attack the entire family, mothers and children together.

questions.question: What can we learn from Jacob mentioning both God’s promise and his fear of Esau?
answers: He trusted God’s promise while also asking for help in danger
He did not believe God’s promise at all
He planned to fight Esau alone
questions.explanation: Jacob recalled God’s promise to multiply his descendants while asking for deliverance from Esau.

questions.question: What does Jacob emphasize by saying, “With my staff I passed over this Jordan; and now I am become two bands”?
answers: That he had never been alone
The change from poverty and simplicity to abundant possessions and family
That he wanted to divide his family permanently
questions.explanation: Jacob recalls crossing the Jordan with only a staff, while now he has many people and possessions divided into two camps.

questions.question: What does “lest he will come and smite me, and the mother with the children” reveal about Jacob’s fear?
answers: He feared that Esau would take only his possessions
He feared that Esau would ask him to return to Haran
He feared the complete destruction of his family, including mothers and children
questions.explanation: Jacob feared that Esau would attack the entire family, mothers and children together.

easy.question: Who sent the gift to Esau?
answers: Jacob
Esau
One of the servants
easy.explanation: Jacob selected animals from his possessions and sent them as a gift to Esau.

easy.question: Where did Jacob stay that night?
answers: On the mountain
In the camp
In Esau’s house
easy.explanation: The passage says that Jacob lodged that night in the camp.

easy.question: Which of the following was included in the gift?
answers: One hundred horses and twenty mules
Thirty sheep and ten goats
Forty cows and ten bulls
easy.explanation: The verse lists forty cows and ten bulls.

medium.question: Why did Jacob command that there be space between each herd?
answers: So that the meeting with the gift and its message would happen gradually
So that the servants would not see one another
So that the animals could return to Jacob
medium.explanation: The separation created a gradual procession, allowing Esau to encounter the gift and Jacob’s message repeatedly.

medium.question: In the phrase “put a space betwixt drove and drove,” what does “space” mean?
answers: Speed
A distance or interval
A gift
medium.explanation: Because it was placed between herds, “space” means a gap or distance.

medium.question: What is the correct order of events?
answers: Jacob met Esau, and then sent the gift
The servants returned to Jacob, and then he divided the herds
Jacob sent the herds ahead, instructed the servants what to say, and stayed behind
medium.explanation: The gift went ahead of Jacob; he then instructed the servants what to say and remained in the camp that night.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from Jacob telling several servants to repeat the same message to Esau?
answers: He wanted the message about the gift and his arrival repeated again and again
He did not know who his servants were
He wanted to hide the gift from Esau
challenge.explanation: The repeated instruction created one consistent, continuing message: the gift was for Esau, and Jacob himself was coming afterward.

challenge.question: In context, what does “perhaps he will accept of me” mean?
answers: Perhaps Esau will lift his face to heaven
Perhaps Esau will receive Jacob favorably and forgive him
Perhaps Esau will hide his face
challenge.explanation: After sending the gift, Jacob hoped that Esau would receive him favorably and be willing to reconcile.

challenge.question: Which detail emphasizes Jacob’s careful planning for the meeting?
answers: Jacob sent all the animals together without order
Jacob told the servants to go ahead but did not tell them what to say
The gift went ahead of Jacob while he stayed in the camp that night
challenge.explanation: The gift went ahead while Jacob remained behind, showing his gradual and cautious preparation for the meeting.

questions.question: What can be inferred from Jacob telling several servants to repeat the same message to Esau?
answers: He wanted the message about the gift and his arrival repeated again and again
He did not know who his servants were
He wanted to hide the gift from Esau
questions.explanation: The repeated instruction created one consistent, continuing message: the gift was for Esau, and Jacob himself was coming afterward.

questions.question: In context, what does “perhaps he will accept of me” mean?
answers: Perhaps Esau will lift his face to heaven
Perhaps Esau will receive Jacob favorably and forgive him
Perhaps Esau will hide his face
questions.explanation: After sending the gift, Jacob hoped that Esau would receive him favorably and be willing to reconcile.

questions.question: Which detail emphasizes Jacob’s careful planning for the meeting?
answers: Jacob sent all the animals together without order
Jacob told the servants to go ahead but did not tell them what to say
The gift went ahead of Jacob while he stayed in the camp that night
questions.explanation: The gift went ahead while Jacob remained behind, showing his gradual and cautious preparation for the meeting.

paragraphs.title: Jacob Moves His Family across the Stream

easy.question: How many children did Jacob have according to the verse?
answers: Ten
Eleven
Twelve
easy.explanation: The verse says, “his eleven sons.”

easy.question: When did Jacob rise and cross the ford of Jabbok?
answers: At night
In the morning
At noon
easy.explanation: The verse begins, “And he rose up that night.”

easy.question: What did Jacob take across the stream?
answers: Only his children
Only his possessions
His family and everything he had
easy.explanation: Jacob sent his wives, servants, and children across, and then sent over everything he had.

medium.question: What is the sequence of events in these verses?
answers: Jacob moved his possessions, and only afterward gathered his family
Jacob took his family across, and then moved his possessions
Jacob met Esau, and then crossed the stream
medium.explanation: Jacob first took his family across and afterward sent over everything he had.

medium.question: Why does the verse say that Jacob sent over “that he had”?
answers: To show that he moved all his possessions, not only his family
To say that he left his family behind
To describe where he slept
medium.explanation: The phrase adds that Jacob also moved all his possessions.

medium.question: What does “womenservants” mean in this context?
answers: His daughters
His female servants
His neighbors
medium.explanation: The word refers to Jacob’s female servants, who are listed with his wives and children.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the verse saying both that Jacob crossed and that he sent them across?
answers: The crossing included Jacob himself and his family
Jacob crossed twice by himself
He did not cross the stream at all
challenge.explanation: The first verb describes Jacob crossing, while the second describes his family being sent across.

challenge.question: How many people are explicitly listed as two wives, two servants, and eleven sons?
answers: Fourteen
Fifteen
Sixteen
challenge.explanation: Two wives plus two servants plus eleven sons equals fifteen people.

challenge.question: What does the word “all” emphasize in “everything he had”?
answers: Only part of his possessions was moved
His possessions remained on the other side
Jacob made sure to move all his possessions
challenge.explanation: The word “all” emphasizes that none of Jacob’s possessions was left behind.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the verse saying both that Jacob crossed and that he sent them across?
answers: The crossing included Jacob himself and his family
Jacob crossed twice by himself
He did not cross the stream at all
questions.explanation: The first verb describes Jacob crossing, while the second describes his family being sent across.

questions.question: How many people are explicitly listed as two wives, two servants, and eleven sons?
answers: Fourteen
Fifteen
Sixteen
questions.explanation: Two wives plus two servants plus eleven sons equals fifteen people.

questions.question: What does the word “all” emphasize in “everything he had”?
answers: Only part of his possessions was moved
His possessions remained on the other side
Jacob made sure to move all his possessions
questions.explanation: The word “all” emphasizes that none of Jacob’s possessions was left behind.

paragraphs.title: The Struggle and the Name Israel

easy.question: Who was left alone at the beginning of the event?
answers: Jacob
Esau
Laban
easy.explanation: The verse says, “And Jacob was left alone.”

easy.question: Which part of Jacob’s body did the man strike?
answers: His shoulder
The hollow of his thigh
His head
easy.explanation: The man touched the hollow of Jacob’s thigh, and it was put out of joint.

easy.question: What did Jacob ask the man to do before letting him go?
answers: Give him water
Tell him his name
Bless him
easy.explanation: Jacob said, “I will not let thee go, except thou bless me.”

medium.question: Why would Jacob not let the man go?
answers: Because he wanted to receive a blessing
Because he wanted to fight until morning
Because he wanted to know the way
medium.explanation: Jacob refused to part from the man until he received a blessing.

medium.question: In context, what does “the hollow of Jacob’s thigh was out of joint” mean?
answers: It was washed in water
It was dislocated or injured
It bent slightly
medium.explanation: The context describes an injury to Jacob’s thigh during the struggle.

medium.question: What was the main change Jacob received as a result of the struggle?
answers: He moved to another city
He received great possessions
His name was changed to Israel
medium.explanation: The man told Jacob, “Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel.”

challenge.question: What can be understood from Jacob’s name being changed to Israel?
answers: The struggle symbolized a change in his status and strength
He forgot his former name
He became younger
challenge.explanation: The name Israel is connected with Jacob’s struggle and victory, expressing a new identity and status.

challenge.question: What unusual detail appears at the end of the encounter?
answers: The man told Jacob his entire history
The man blessed Jacob without revealing his name
Jacob blessed the man before parting
challenge.explanation: Jacob asked the man’s name, but the man did not answer directly; instead, he blessed Jacob.

challenge.question: What is the connection between daybreak and the man’s request, “Let me go”?
answers: Daybreak caused Jacob to fall asleep
Daybreak showed that the struggle was just beginning
Daybreak signaled that it was time to end the encounter
challenge.explanation: The man asked to be released because day was breaking, suggesting that the morning marked the end of the struggle.

questions.question: What can be understood from Jacob’s name being changed to Israel?
answers: The struggle symbolized a change in his status and strength
He forgot his former name
He became younger
questions.explanation: The name Israel is connected with Jacob’s struggle and victory, expressing a new identity and status.

questions.question: What unusual detail appears at the end of the encounter?
answers: The man told Jacob his entire history
The man blessed Jacob without revealing his name
Jacob blessed the man before parting
questions.explanation: Jacob asked the man’s name, but the man did not answer directly; instead, he blessed Jacob.

questions.question: What is the connection between daybreak and the man’s request, “Let me go”?
answers: Daybreak caused Jacob to fall asleep
Daybreak showed that the struggle was just beginning
Daybreak signaled that it was time to end the encounter
questions.explanation: The man asked to be released because day was breaking, suggesting that the morning marked the end of the struggle.

easy.question: Who named the place?
answers: Jacob
Esau
Moses
easy.explanation: The verse says, “And Jacob called the name of the place Peniel.”

easy.question: What name did Jacob give the place?
answers: Bethel
Peniel
Mahanaim
easy.explanation: Jacob called the place Peniel.

easy.question: Whom did Jacob say he had seen face to face?
answers: Esau
An angel of the LORD
God
easy.explanation: Jacob said, “I have seen God face to face.”

medium.question: Why did Jacob call the place “Peniel”?
answers: Because he said he had seen God there face to face
Because it was where he lived
Because he met Esau there
medium.explanation: Jacob explained the name by saying that he had seen God face to face.

medium.question: What connection does Jacob make between seeing God and the preservation of his life?
answers: Jacob immediately fled the place
Despite the awesome encounter, his life was preserved
Jacob was unsure whom he had seen
medium.explanation: Jacob mentions both seeing God and the fact that his life was preserved.

medium.question: What does “my life is preserved” mean?
answers: My life was forgotten
My life was hidden
I was rescued and remained alive
medium.explanation: The phrase means that Jacob survived the danger of the encounter and remained alive.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from Jacob’s words, “my life is preserved”?
answers: Jacob thought that such an encounter could endanger a person
Jacob considered the encounter unimportant
Jacob wanted to hide the place
challenge.explanation: Emphasizing the preservation of his life suggests that Jacob viewed the encounter as exceedingly dangerous or awe-inspiring.

challenge.question: What linguistic connection stands out between “Peniel” and Jacob’s words?
answers: The name is related to the word “life”
The name is related to “face” and seeing God
The name is related to the word “place”
challenge.explanation: The name Peniel is associated with “face,” matching Jacob’s explanation that he saw God face to face.

challenge.question: What does the verse chiefly emphasize?
answers: Jacob’s journey to a new place
The name of the person Jacob met
The name of the place and the reason Jacob gave for it
challenge.explanation: The verse focuses on the name Peniel and Jacob’s explanation of that name.

questions.question: What can be inferred from Jacob’s words, “my life is preserved”?
answers: Jacob thought that such an encounter could endanger a person
Jacob considered the encounter unimportant
Jacob wanted to hide the place
questions.explanation: Emphasizing the preservation of his life suggests that Jacob viewed the encounter as exceedingly dangerous or awe-inspiring.

questions.question: What linguistic connection stands out between “Peniel” and Jacob’s words?
answers: The name is related to the word “life”
The name is related to “face” and seeing God
The name is related to the word “place”
questions.explanation: The name Peniel is associated with “face,” matching Jacob’s explanation that he saw God face to face.

questions.question: What does the verse chiefly emphasize?
answers: Jacob’s journey to a new place
The name of the person Jacob met
The name of the place and the reason Jacob gave for it
questions.explanation: The verse focuses on the name Peniel and Jacob’s explanation of that name.

paragraphs.title: The Sun Rises and Jacob Walks with a Limp

easy.question: What rose for Jacob?
answers: The sun
The moon
The stars
easy.explanation: The verse says, “The sun rose upon him.”

easy.question: When did the sun rise?
answers: Before Jacob reached Penuel
As Jacob passed over Penuel
The night before
easy.explanation: The verse says that the sun rose as Jacob passed over Penuel.

easy.question: Which part of his body did Jacob limp on?
answers: His hand
His shoulder
His thigh
easy.explanation: The verse ends by saying that Jacob halted upon his thigh.

medium.question: What can be understood about Jacob’s condition after he passed Penuel?
answers: He was injured or in pain and therefore limped
He was happy and danced
He lay down and could not move
medium.explanation: His limp shows that Jacob’s physical condition was difficult or painful.

medium.question: What does “halted upon his thigh” mean?
answers: He ran quickly
He walked with a limp because of pain or injury
He slept on his side
medium.explanation: The phrase means that he walked abnormally, evidently because of the injury to his thigh.

medium.question: What sequence of events is described in the verse?
answers: Jacob limped, passed Penuel, and then the sun rose
The sun rose, Jacob reached Penuel, and then he limped
Jacob passed Penuel, the sun rose, and he limped upon his thigh
medium.explanation: The verse says that Jacob passed Penuel, the sun rose, and he was limping on his thigh.

challenge.question: What contrast stands out in the verse?
answers: Between Penuel and the thigh
Between sun and night
Between the rising sun and Jacob’s weakness
challenge.explanation: The rising sun suggests light and renewal, while Jacob was still injured and limping.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the verse mentioning both Penuel and Jacob’s limp?
answers: The event at Penuel affected Jacob’s physical condition
Jacob remained sleeping at Penuel
The sun caused Jacob to limp
challenge.explanation: The verse connects Jacob’s passing from Penuel with his limp, suggesting that his condition resulted from the preceding event.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “the sun rose upon him” emphasize?
answers: That the sun rose only at night
That the sunrise is described in relation to Jacob and his condition
That the sun rose somewhere else
challenge.explanation: The wording presents the sunrise as an experience connected with Jacob as he passed Penuel.

questions.question: What contrast stands out in the verse?
answers: Between Penuel and the thigh
Between sun and night
Between the rising sun and Jacob’s weakness
questions.explanation: The rising sun suggests light and renewal, while Jacob was still injured and limping.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the verse mentioning both Penuel and Jacob’s limp?
answers: The event at Penuel affected Jacob’s physical condition
Jacob remained sleeping at Penuel
The sun caused Jacob to limp
questions.explanation: The verse connects Jacob’s passing from Penuel with his limp, suggesting that his condition resulted from the preceding event.

questions.question: What does the phrase “the sun rose upon him” emphasize?
answers: That the sun rose only at night
That the sunrise is described in relation to Jacob and his condition
That the sun rose somewhere else
questions.explanation: The wording presents the sunrise as an experience connected with Jacob as he passed Penuel.

paragraphs.title: A Memorial of the Injury to the Thigh

easy.question: What do the children of Israel not eat?
answers: The sinew that shrank
The hollow of the thigh
All meat
easy.explanation: The verse explicitly says that the children of Israel do not eat the sinew that shrank.

easy.question: Who observes the prohibition mentioned in the verse?
answers: The children of Esau
The children of Israel
The shepherds
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Therefore the children of Israel eat not.”

easy.question: Which part of Jacob’s body was touched and injured?
answers: His shoulder
His hand
The hollow of his thigh
easy.explanation: The verse says that the man touched the hollow of Jacob’s thigh.

medium.question: Why do the children of Israel not eat the sinew that shrank?
answers: It had been forbidden since the creation of the world
Because the man touched the hollow of Jacob’s thigh
Because it is found only in certain animals
medium.explanation: The verse explains the prohibition by saying that the man touched the hollow of Jacob’s thigh.

medium.question: What does “Therefore the children of Israel eat not” mean in context?
answers: For this reason, they do not eat it
Perhaps they will eat it
They have already eaten it
medium.explanation: “Therefore” connects Jacob’s injury with the prohibition.

medium.question: What does “unto this day” indicate about the prohibition?
answers: The prohibition lasted only that day
The prohibition began before Jacob
The prohibition continued until the time the verse was written or transmitted
medium.explanation: The phrase indicates that the practice was still observed at the time referred to by the verse.

challenge.question: What connection does the verse make between an event involving Jacob and the children of Israel?
answers: Jacob’s injury became the reason for a practice observed by all Israel
The children of Israel injured their own thighs
Jacob forbade Esau’s descendants to eat
challenge.explanation: The verse connects Jacob’s personal injury with an eating prohibition observed by the children of Israel.

challenge.question: What precise detail does the verse emphasize about the sinew?
answers: It is upon the hollow of the thigh
It is found in the head
It is found in the palm of the hand
challenge.explanation: The verse describes the sinew as being upon the hollow of the thigh.

challenge.question: Why can the prohibition be understood as a memorial of an event involving Jacob?
answers: Because the sinew is said to be found in every person
Because the verse explains the prohibition by Jacob’s injured thigh
Because the verse says the prohibition is for health
challenge.explanation: The verse gives no medical reason; it explicitly connects the prohibition with Jacob’s injury.

questions.question: What connection does the verse make between an event involving Jacob and the children of Israel?
answers: Jacob’s injury became the reason for a practice observed by all Israel
The children of Israel injured their own thighs
Jacob forbade Esau’s descendants to eat
questions.explanation: The verse connects Jacob’s personal injury with an eating prohibition observed by the children of Israel.

questions.question: What precise detail does the verse emphasize about the sinew?
answers: It is upon the hollow of the thigh
It is found in the head
It is found in the palm of the hand
questions.explanation: The verse describes the sinew as being upon the hollow of the thigh.

questions.question: Why can the prohibition be understood as a memorial of an event involving Jacob?
answers: Because the sinew is said to be found in every person
Because the verse explains the prohibition by Jacob’s injured thigh
Because the verse says the prohibition is for health
questions.explanation: The verse gives no medical reason; it explicitly connects the prohibition with Jacob’s injury.
